title: CodeScout: An Effective Recipe for Reinforcement Learning of Code Search Agents
relevance_note: CodeScout: An Effective Recipe for Reinforcement Learning of Code Search Agents is a paper source with details on terminal only localization, localization finish schema relevant to execution control.
reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on execution loop, tool gateway, verification.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper frames code localization as the first step in issue resolution and reports that relying on general-purpose models for localization inside the coding loop can cause high costs, incorrect fixes, and code bloat.

CodeScout uses a bash-only scaffold with standard Unix commands such as `rg`, `find`, `ls`, `grep`, and `sed`, plus a `LocalizationFinish` tool whose structured schema improved reward-signal fidelity over brittle string outputs.

During training, agents often exhausted the step budget without submitting predictions; adding a binary reward for terminating exactly at the step limit mitigated collapse, while auxiliary rewards for parallel tool-calling hurt performance and were replaced by explicit prompting.
